clue.text: Lovely cleaner of high-quality porcelain

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a cleaning lady
Ming porcelain, from China's Ming dynasty, is famously fine

explanation.surface: Praise for a domestic help who looks after the valuable Chinese vases.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and lovely are synonyms, both describing something delightful or attractive.

clue.text: Difficult to hide ring in collection

indicators.note: the word for difficult hides the ring shape within it

parts.note: hard means difficult
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: It's hard to conceal a ring among a set of items.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stored stockpile or cache, such as a hidden collection of treasure.

clue.text: Man bringing a bit of sunshine

definitions.meaning: a ... is a single beam of light, as in a ... of sunshine

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow brightening the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray is a male first name and also a narrow beam of light.

clue.text: Native home on Scottish island son escapes from

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the son letter escapes, leaving the island's name

parts.note: Uist (North and South) is in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A local person's son runs away from his house on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous peoples of the Arctic, so native inhabitants there.

clue.text: Drink stuff — stiff stuff!

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or any alcoholic drink
to stuff is to ram something in

explanation.surface: Knock back the booze — strong stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' suggests a strong drink, but grogram is a coarse, stiffened fabric, and 'stuff' is an old word for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grogram is a coarse fabric of silk mixed with mohair or wool, often stiffened with gum.

clue.text: There's little good in lad who is a malign influence?

indicators.note: the small letter for good is placed in the middle of the word for a lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy
G is a short form, a little version, of good

explanation.surface: A worried remark that a boy has no goodness in him and is a bad influence.
explanation.walkthrough: A bogy (or bogey) is something feared or troublesome; the question mark flags the looser definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogy is an object of dread or an evil spirit, so a malign presence or influence.

clue.text: Bishop leading the French chants offers benedictions

indicators.note: the bishop letter leads, coming first in the answer

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
les is French for the (plural)
chants means sings

explanation.surface: A bishop heads French choristers who sing out blessings.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedictions are prayers invoking divine favour, which is what blessings are.

clue.text: Enraged drunk — one may explode

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An angry drunk is a person liable to blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand that bursts on detonation.

clue.text: Cautious in conflict, coming to enemy finally

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of enemy

explanation.surface: Someone is careful during a war when the enemy at last arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wary is to be on guard, a direct synonym of being careful or cautious.

clue.text: Like problematic jar of marmalade? End up with one chucked!

indicators.note: letters chucked about are thrown into disorder, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frustrating breakfast moment: the marmalade jar won't open, so you end up throwing it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked' looks like throwing the jar out, but it is the anagram signal on END UP ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar whose lid will not come off remains sealed, which is the cheeky example the question mark flags.

clue.text: One praising novel art aloud

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

explanation.surface: Someone enthusing about new art by speaking it aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aloud' suggests a homophone, but here it is simply part of the anagram fodder with ART.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulator heaps flattery or excessive praise on someone, so is one who praises.

clue.text: Letters descend on crickets's HQ

parts.note: to land is to come down
Lord's, in London, is the home of English cricket

explanation.surface: Mail arrives at the headquarters of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like post but means people who let property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord lets property to tenants, so landlords are, whimsically, those who let.

clue.text: Remain to offer support

definitions.meaning: a prop or brace, as in a ship's rigging or a corset

explanation.surface: Someone decides not to leave so as to be of help.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay is both a verb for staying put and a noun for a supporting rope or strut.

clue.text: Star perhaps getting a black eye

definitions.meaning: a star is something that shines
slang for a bruised black eye

explanation.surface: A celebrity ends up with a bruised face, perhaps after a scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A star gives off light and so is a thing that shines; separately, slang names a bruised eye this way.

clue.text: Pay absolute attention to new author taking in English

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in, holds, the English letter
new indicates a new arrangement of the letters of author

explanation.surface: Listen closely to a fresh writer who brings in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes HAROUT from AUTHOR; 'taking in' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear someone out is to listen to everything they have to say without interrupting.

clue.text: What old lawn needs to be, we hear? It's faded

indicators.note: we hear tells us to listen to how the phrase sounds

parts.words: What old lawn needs to be
parts.note: a tired lawn needs to be sown with seed again

explanation.surface: A gardener thinks a tired lawn needs work, as it has lost its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Receded means withdrew or diminished, which is close to faded away.

clue.text: Entertained by churchmen, delightful scientific monk

indicators.note: the answer is entertained, held within, the words churchmen delightful

explanation.surface: Clergymen play host to a charming monk who does science.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregor Mendel was an Augustinian friar whose pea experiments founded genetics.

clue.text: Everyone at the back of hotel room

indicators.note: everyone's word comes at the back of, after, the hotel letter

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
everyone means all

explanation.surface: All the guests have gathered at the rear of a hotel's room.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall is a large room for gatherings, or an entrance passage in a house.

clue.text: I'm so funny in fancy lace garment

indicators.note: one rearranged group of letters goes in the middle of the other
fancy here means fancifully rearranged, so lace's letters are reordered
funny means odd, so the letters of I'm so are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone finds themselves amusing wearing an elaborate lace item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'fancy' works on LACE and 'funny' on I'M SO, and 'in' sets the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless undergarment for the upper body, a type of clothing.

clue.text: Mum's working for a member of a secret society

parts.note: ma is mum, so ma's is mum's
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Mother is busy on behalf of one belonging to a secret society.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mason, or Freemason, belongs to the fraternal order often called secretive.

clue.text: Composer's final jazz piece included in catalogue

definitions.note: the clue's Composer's stands for Composer is, so the definition plus a contracted verb links it to the wordplay; the answer is a single noun

indicators.note: the selected letter is included within the catalogue word

parts.note: a catalogue is a list

indicators.note: final asks for the last letter of jazz

explanation.surface: A composer's last jazz work appears in a catalogue of his music.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Card some organised for colleagues

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A greetings card has been arranged for workmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Comrades are companions or fellow members, close in sense to colleagues.

clue.text: Show contempt for hospital food

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for disrespecting them
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient sneers at the meals served in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food, as in a favourite dish.

clue.text: End of crossword — I am needing a bit of illumination?

indicators.note: end of asks for the last letter of crossword

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: A solver at the end of the crossword wants a little enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illumination' seems to mean insight, but the definition is literal: lacking light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dim is poorly lit, so it could do with more light.

clue.text: Greek characters sat back after end of voyage

indicators.note: the reversed word comes after the single letter
end of asks for the last letter of voyage
back means the word sat is read backwards

explanation.surface: Greeks sitting back after a long voyage ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet; the plural gives letters, or characters.

clue.text: Tiny dame, surprisingly explosive

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A small woman turns out to have an explosive temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' reads as describing the dame but is a noun naming the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is a blasting explosive invented by Alfred Nobel.
